scope: Read-only source/anchor audit. Initial six-generation anchor analysis plus explicitly requested P4 consistency follow-up using narrowly registered archive reads. No media edits, paid generation, key reads, API calls, commits or motion-status changes.
conclusion: Two deliberately different input-color schemes. All eleven PNGs match receipt hashes. Start-to-end changes are bounded to added target polygons; magenta preparation deliberately also recolors the stationary centre card. Color is not physical-side proof.

findings.title: Two explicit color schemes, not corrupt files
findings.detail: P6 turn-01 and P7 turn-01/02/03 use yellow shoe-card back plus blue existing/front target. P7 pink-01 and direct-01 use exact magenta tracking cores on all visible cards. All eleven stored input files match their generation receipt SHA-256 values.

findings.title: End anchor adds only one target; next shoe card retains start color
findings.detail: All five end anchors differ from start only within the registered new-card polygon. No other source RGB pixels change, including hand/body, shoe housing, shoe-card face and existing centre card. The retained shoe card represents the next card; the new landing card is a separate object.

findings.title: Pink preparation also recolors the existing centre card
findings.detail: The shared pink start is derived from the exact yellow/blue source anchor. It deliberately changes 4,555 shoe-card pixels and 5,050 existing-centre-card pixels to RGB 255,0,255. Zero pixels outside the registered input-mask change. This is a preparation-stage appearance change, not a physical turn or card movement.

findings.title: P7 turn-03 returned to yellow/blue after two pink requests
findings.detail: The generator explicitly selects P7 turn-02/start.png for --turn and requests YELLOW BACK / BLUE FRONT. Its request followed pink-01 and direct-01. Motion metadata documents that the source was already submitted before Jakob clarified that pink remained the mask method. It is an original recorded request, not a later image replacement. Future pink mask policy therefore should not be inferred from the latest historical input.

findings.title: Blue is not one exact RGB in these input images
findings.detail: P6 turn-01 and P7 turn-02 add RGB 0,0,255. P7 turn-03 adds RGB 7,90,216 (#075ad8), explicitly selected in the generator. The preserved source centre card is shaded blue, with representative modal core RGB 0,94,224. Both target colors meet the prompt word BLUE, but they are not interchangeable exact label masks. No rationale for the shade change is recorded.

findings.title: Prior motion reviews record actual output defects
findings.detail: P7 turn-01: wrong landing/blue shoe and wrong visible-side coloring. P7 turn-02: BACK→FRONT→BACK, front colored yellow and back landing colored blue. P6 turn-01: LH→RH transfer and printed face. P7 turn-03: premature P7 card, held-card landing near P4, blue shoe. Direct-01: CLOSED→CLOSED despite requested turn, retained only as secondary motion. These are existing registered decisions, not a fresh video-side certification.
findings.source: Each motions/<id>.json review and observed fields, preserved below.

findings.title: Static anchors cannot establish physical-side success
findings.detail: Pink-01 and turn-03 physical end side/turn count remain UNKNOWN in the registry. Direct-01 is reported BACK→BACK. None of the static image checks certifies a physical turnover, contact, return cut or Scout integration. Provider-side received PNG bytes were not independently retrieved.

findings.title: P7 turn-01 has a start image only
findings.detail: The receipt has no end field and the directory contains no end.png. The absence is an original single-anchor request, not an observed missing/mutated second-anchor hash.

findings.title: P4 review-v04 colors the revealed blue source face yellow
findings.detail: Same local/archive source e3b38f89… shows an opposite surface after f61–62 edge; diagnostic code forces moving blue pixels to yellow. At f68 fixed moving-card ROI: 2,424 blue source pixels, 2,004 become yellow and zero remain blue (others are contour/compression/mixed pixels). CLOSED→CLOSED metadata is not independent proof; see p4Followup.

motions.promptText: Locked camera, continuous six-second shot between these exact anchors. Same woman, left hand on SCREEN RIGHT, green studio and black shoe. A single rigid card has a YELLOW BACK and BLUE FRONT. At the outlet yellow is UP and blue is DOWN. Left index and middle fingers start ON TOP of yellow; thumb is underneath. Pull one card just clear of the outlet. Perform an UNDERHAND TURNOVER while moving directly to the lower-right landing spot: rotate the left forearm from PALM DOWN to PALM UP, turning the card over 180 degrees around its long edge. The yellow upper surface visibly rotates DOWN through an edge-on moment, revealing the blue underside, which becomes the UPWARD face. Finish the rotation with index and middle fingers UNDER the card supporting its yellow underside, and thumb above its blue face. Keep that palm-up grip until placement. Lower the card BLUE FACE UP at the new position in the last image and slide the supporting fingers OUT FROM UNDER it. Do not turn the wrist palm-down again until AFTER releasing the card. No palm pressing on top, no second turnover, no flat spin, no colour morph. One physical card, one turnover. Stay beside the shoe, no centre detour or hand transfer. By 5.3s return the empty left hand to its exact original shoe-ready pose and settle. The new blue card and old centre blue card remain still; the next shoe card stays yellow. Preserve natural gaze, fingers and framing.

f68PixelVerification.method: Decode same frame and fixed ROI from source and diagnostic MP4 into memory. Blue: B>65, B-R>42, B-G>22. Yellow: R/G>160 and B<min(R,G)*0.4. ROI excludes stationary C1 and shoe. No frame files saved.
